resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO); Certificate of Transfer of Title (CTT) for vacant or rehab properties
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Lindenwold Construction Office / Code Enforcement (Housing Clerk)
resale_co.lead_time: Borough Code 105-13.1 says apply not less than 10 business days before the scheduled closing; the inspection is to happen within 5 days of the application. The fee is lower when the inspection is scheduled 10 or more business days out. For a vacant CTT, apply at least 10 days before settlement.
resale_co.valid_for: 90 days from issuance (Borough Code 105-13.1); may be extended up to another 90 days if the owner certifies in writing that nothing has changed
requirements: No open building or zoning permits (must be closed with fees paid)
No work done without a required construction or zoning permit
No unsafe structures or unsafe conditions
10-year sealed battery smoke alarm on every level and outside each sleeping area
CO alarm within 10 feet of sleeping areas
2A-10B:C fire extinguisher under 10 lbs, mounted within 10 ft of kitchen, tagged with current receipt (form still lists it)
House numbers at least 4 inches, contrasting, fixed to the house and visible from the street
Handrails on 3 or more risers; guardrails on porches/decks 30 inches or higher
GFCI within 6 ft of water; no bare-wire fixtures
Heat, appliances (anti-tip on range), hot and cold water and toilets working
Water heater relief valve discharge pipe 2 to 6 inches from floor
Bathroom window or exhaust fan
No holes, flaking paint or water stains on walls, ceilings, floors; no roof leaks
Yard free of trash, debris and junk vehicles; all code violations abated
Utilities on at time of inspection

fees.label: CCO inspection, 1-2 units, scheduled over 10 days out (form: 10 or more business days), per unit
fees.quote: (1) Inspection of property scheduled over 10 days: $75.

fees.label: CCO inspection, scheduled less than 10 days out (form: 4 to 10 business days), per unit
fees.quote: Inspection of property scheduled less than 10 days: $100.

fees.label: Administration fee for changing inspection date or unit number more than once
fees.quote: (3) Administration fee to be assessed for any change of inspection date or unit number more than once and that fees must be paid before a change is made: $20.

fees.label: Certificate of Transfer of Title (vacant property), includes one re-inspection within 120 days
fees.quote: (4) Property title transfer (Vacant): $125 includes one re-inspection fee within 120 days of new ownership.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the one-page CCO application and submit it to the Code Enforcement Office at 15 N. White Horse Pike with a check or money order payable to the Borough of Lindenwold. Fees are per unit and nonrefundable. The Borough calls the listed contact to schedule after the permit and zoning search is done. A failed inspection needs a new application and fee before reinspection. For vacant or rehab properties, file the CTT and the CCO at the same time.

evidence.quote: All sales of a property must file for a certificate of occupancy (C/O) inspection for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors, fire extinguishers, and house numbers.
The new inspection requirement is required for the sale or transfer of any Residential Dwelling.
ONE TO TWO UNITS - FAMILY DWELLING RESALE INSPECTION APPLICATION CONTINUED CERTIFICATION OF OCCUPANCY
Once property has been inspected and approval for sale, the associated Continued Certification of Occupancy shall generally be issued the next business day.
When applying for the CTT (Certificate of Transfer of Title) you must also apply for the CCO (Continued Certification of Occupancy) at the same time.

No person shall convey title to any residential property in the Borough of Lindenwold, consisting of 15 dwelling units or less without first obtaining a continued certification of occupancy for each unit in the manner herein provided
Such continued certification of occupancy shall be valid for a period of 90 days from the date of its issuance, after which ninety-day period it shall expire.

resale_co.notes: Re-checked October 20, 2026; the Borough page and the CCO and CTT forms (modified August 2023) are unchanged. The Borough code (Chapter 105, read on ecode360) requires a continued certification of occupancy before title to a residential property of 15 units or less is conveyed. Exempt: transfers to an existing owner of record, to an immediate family member of the grantor (grandparents, spouses, children, grandchildren), or to a trust for immediate family. The code also says the CCO fee includes the smoke detector inspection fee, and a new section 150-28.1 (Ord. No. 2025-09) adds a separate smoke/CO certificate fee collected by the Fire District (see fire certificate). Code 150-28C repeats the $75 / $100 / $20 / $125 fees on the form, so they are not listed twice. Program took effect October 1, 2020. The form lists no tier for under 4 business days. Inspection takes about 15 to 30 minutes. The Borough CCO checklist also covers smoke/CO alarms, the extinguisher and house numbers, separate from the Fire District certificate. Rental registration and new-tenant inspection are separate rental programs.
resale_co.contact_title: Office Manager, Code Enforcement / Housing (ext. 225); Housing Clerk at ext. 224

requirements: 10-year sealed battery smoke alarm on every level; hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement alarm at bottom of stairwell on the ceiling, not between joists
Bedroom hallway smoke alarms within 10 feet of all bedroom doors
Smoke and CO alarms less than 10 years old and working
CO alarm in hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms; not in switched outlets
Low-voltage alarm systems must be tested by an alarm contractor before the inspection, with the certificate shown to the inspector
House numbers at least 4 inches, contrasting, fixed to the house, visible from the street or 50 feet (Borough Ordinance No. 757)
Homes with a secondary power source (solar, generator, battery storage) need a permanent printed label at the main panel and meter, e.g. "Caution: Multiple Sources of Power"

authorities.name: Lindenwold Fire District No. 1, Bureau of Fire Prevention
authorities.lead_time: Submit request 3 to 4 weeks before settlement

fees.label: Request received 8 or more calendar days before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received eight (8) calendar days or more prior to the settlement date: $45.00

fees.label: Request received 7 calendar days before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received seven (7) calendar days prior to the settlement date: $90.00

fees.label: Request received 3 calendar days or less before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received three (3) calendar days or less prior to the settlement date: $161.00

authorities.how_to_apply: Submit the online Residential Inspection Request Form on lindenwoldfire.com. Pay at the time of inspection by check or money order (no cash). The certificate is issued at the inspection if the home passes and payment is received. No temporary certificates.

evidence.quote: When selling a one or two family home in Lindenwold, you must obtain a Certificate of Smoke Alarm and Carbon Monoxide Detector Compliance CSACMAPFEC 5:70-2.3 (a) prior to the settlement. Please submit your request for inspection 3 to 4 weeks prior to the settlement date.
Payment is due at the time of inspection - check or money order payable to Lindenwold Fire District. NO CASH IS ACCEPTED Temporary certificates are NOT issued.
Requests must be submitted using the online form located at www.lindenwoldfire.com, 3 to 4 weeks prior to the settlement date.
The fees charged pursuant to this section shall be collected by Lindenwold Fire District No. 1 and paid to the Bureau of Fire Prevention.

The fees charged herein shall be charged in addition to the fees as required by §150-28, and shall only be charged for an application for a Certificate of Occupancy for structures used, or intended to be used, for residential purposes by not more than two households.

fire_cert.notes: New this round: Borough Ordinance No. 2025-09 (Oct 8, 2025) added Code 150-28.1, which sets the smoke/CO certificate fee at $45 (more than 10 business days), $90 (4 to 10 business days) and $161 (fewer than 4 business days) before the change of occupant, charged on top of the Borough CCO fee and collected by Lindenwold Fire District No. 1. The Fire District's own fee sheet (scanned July 2026, read by eye) uses calendar days instead: $45 for 8 or more days, $90 for 7 days, $161 for 3 days or less, plus a $50 reinspection. The amounts match but the day cutoffs differ; the code's 4 to 10 business day tier covers the 4 to 6 day gap on the sheet. Both sets are listed. The web page says checks payable to 'Lindenwold Fire District'; the sheet says 'Lindenwold Fire Department'. Certificate valid 90 days. Fire Official: Timothy Shannon (tshannon@lindenwoldfire.com). The NJ DCA fire directory still lists the smoke detector compliance contact as 'Lindenwold Boro', 2001 Egg Harbor Rd., (856) 783-2121, which looks out of date; the Borough code and the Fire District site both say the Fire District issues and collects for the certificate. The Borough's 2020 Smoke Instructions sheet (scanned) and the CCO checklist still list a 2A-10B:C extinguisher; the Fire District checklist has none, in line with P.L.2025, c.19, but the code section title still says CSACMAPFEC (portable fire extinguisher).

other_items.label: Open permits must be closed
other_items.detail: No open building or zoning permits; must be fully satisfied with fees and inspections before the CCO is issued.

other_items.label: Work without permits
other_items.detail: Unpermitted work (commonly finished basements, water heaters, furnaces) must be permitted and inspected before the CCO is issued.

other_items.label: Zoning check
other_items.detail: The Borough runs a zoning approval and permit search before scheduling the CCO inspection.
